problems.title: Equivalent product and quotient inequalities
problems.question: Which are equivalent: I (x−19)(x−199)≤0; II the same product <0; III (x−19)/(x−199)≤0; IV the same quotient <0?
problems.idea: Compare the exact solution intervals, including endpoints.
formulas: Product is negative between its roots; the quotient is undefined at 199.
steps: I gives [19,199], II gives (19,199), III gives [19,199), IV gives (19,199).
Only II and IV have identical solution sets.

problems.title: Intersect two solution sets
problems.question: A solves (x−3)/(x−1)≤0 and B solves |x−3|≥x−1. Find A∩B.
problems.idea: Solve each inequality before intersecting.
steps: For x≤3, the second inequality is 3−x≥x−1, hence x≤2. For x>3 it would require −3≥−1, impossible.
The common part is (1,2].

problems.title: Range of a quadratic on a closed interval
problems.question: Find the range of y=x²−4x+12 for −1≤x≤3.
problems.idea: Complete the square and check the vertex and endpoints.
steps: The minimum is 8 at x=2. Endpoint values are 17 at −1 and 9 at 3.
Continuity gives every value between the minimum and maximum.

problems.title: Area from two sides and their angle bisector
problems.question: Adjacent sides are 28 and 21; the included-angle bisector is 12√2. Find the area.
problems.idea: The bisector determines half the included angle.
steps: 24cos(A/2)=12√2 gives A/2=45°, hence A=90°.

problems.title: Choose the longer third side
problems.question: Two triangle sides are 3 and 2√2, area 3. Find the third side, which is greater than both.
problems.idea: The area determines the sine of the included angle, allowing an acute or obtuse case.
steps: A=45° gives a²=5; A=135° gives a²=29.
Only √29 exceeds both known sides.

problems.title: Equivalent absolute-value inequalities
problems.question: Which are equivalent: I x²≤|x|; II x≤1; III x²≤1; IV x≤|x|?
problems.idea: Replace |x| by a nonnegative variable in I.
steps: I gives [−1,1], exactly the solution of III.
II gives (−∞,1], while IV holds for every real x.

problems.title: Locate a parabola’s vertex
problems.question: Where is the vertex of y=x²−66x+1089?
problems.idea: Recognize a square.
steps: The vertex is (33,0).

problems.title: Equal values of a quadratic
problems.question: A nonconstant quadratic satisfies f(−3)=f(7). Find x with f(x)=f(x+2).
problems.idea: Equal values lie symmetrically about the axis.
steps: The midpoint of x and x+2 must equal 2: x+1=2.

problems.title: Sine of a rhombus angle
problems.question: A rhombus has diagonals 16 and 12. Find the sine of its acute angle.
problems.idea: Calculate its area in two ways.
steps: Thus sinθ=96/100.

problems.title: Area bands cut by parallels
problems.question: Two points divide AB in ratio 1:2:3 from A. Lines through them parallel to BC divide the triangle into three regions. Find their area ratio from A.
problems.idea: Similar-triangle areas scale as squared lengths.
steps: Cumulative area units are 1,9,36.
Subtract successive totals to obtain region areas 1,8,27.

problems.title: An increasing quadratic on an interval
problems.question: Which listed a makes y=ax²−6x+2 increasing on [2,4]?
problems.idea: Its slope must be nonnegative throughout that interval.
formulas: Slope=2ax−6. For a>0 its minimum on [2,4] is 4a−6.
steps: We need a≥3/2. For a≤0 the slope is negative there.
Among 0,2,√2/2,1,√2,1/2, only 2 qualifies.

problems.title: Match two monotonicity intervals
problems.question: When does the increasing interval of x²−ax+199 equal the decreasing interval of ax²−4x+199?
problems.idea: The second parabola must open downward to have a right-hand decreasing interval.
formulas: First interval starts at a/2; for a<0 the second starts at 2/a.
steps: Equate a/2=2/a to get a²=4.
Retain only the negative value.

problems.title: A midpoint inequality determines concavity
problems.question: For f(x)=ax²+bx+c, f(1)+f(3)<2f(2). What follows?
problems.idea: Expand the difference; the linear terms cancel.
steps: The hypothesis is 2a<0.

problems.title: Area from two heights and their angle
problems.question: A parallelogram’s heights from one vertex are 5 and 12, with sin of their angle 1/3. Find the area.
problems.idea: The sine of the angle between the heights equals the sine between the sides.
formulas: If S=ab sinθ, then h₁=b sinθ,h₂=a sinθ, so S=h₁h₂/sinθ.

problems.title: Product of inradius and circumradius
problems.question: Triangle sides are 18,19,20. Find rR.
problems.idea: The area cancels in the two radius formulas.

problems.title: A polynomial whose domain equals its range
problems.question: For which a does f(x)=ax²+(2a+1)x+a+2 have the same domain and range?
problems.idea: Its domain is all real numbers; a genuine quadratic has a one-sided bounded range.
steps: For a≠0 a quadratic cannot have range all real numbers.
At a=0 the linear function takes every real value.

problems.title: Minimize a weighted sum of squares
problems.question: a+b=14, and 2a²+5b² is minimal. Find 2a+5b.
problems.idea: Complete the square after substituting b=14−a.
steps: The minimum occurs at a=10,b=4.

problems.title: Count integer solutions of an absolute-value inequality
problems.question: How many integers solve |x²−2x−3|<3x+3?
problems.idea: Use both strict inequalities and intersect.
steps: The left inequality becomes x(x+1)>0, giving x<−1 or x>0.
The right becomes (x−6)(x+1)<0, giving −1<x<6.
Together 0<x<6, with integers 1,2,3,4,5.

problems.title: A right triangle’s hypotenuse tangency segments
problems.question: An incircle divides a right triangle’s hypotenuse into 3 and 10. Find the area.
problems.idea: Equal tangent segments at the right vertex have length r.
steps: Pythagoras gives (3+r)²+(10+r)²=169, or r²+13r−30=0.
The positive root is r=2, so the legs are 5 and 12.

problems.title: Area with hypotenuse 8 and an angle 15 degrees
problems.question: A right triangle has hypotenuse 8 and acute angle 15°. Find its area.
problems.idea: Use the double-angle identity.

problems.title: Largest rectangle perimeter under a parabola
problems.question: A rectangle has two vertices on the x-axis and the other two on y=4−x² in the first and second quadrants. Find the greatest perimeter.
problems.idea: Let the upper vertices have opposite coordinates ±t.
steps: For 0<t<2 the square is minimized at t=1.
The width is 2 and the height 3, giving perimeter 10.

problems.title: A rational sign chart with even powers
problems.question: Count integer solutions of [(x−6)⁶(x²−8x+15)(x−2)⁴(x−8)]/[(x−7)⁵(x²−5x+4)(x²−4x+4)]≤0.
problems.idea: Factor the quadratics; even powers do not change signs but zeros and exclusions matter.
formulas: Exclude 1,2,4,7. Away from zeros the sign is that of (x−3)(x−5)(x−8)/[(x−7)(x−1)(x−4)].
steps: The nonpositive intervals are (1,3], (4,5], (7,8], with excluded points removed.
They contribute integers 3,5,8. In addition x=6 makes the even-power numerator zero and is allowed.

problems.title: Count integers between irrational roots
problems.question: How many integers solve x²+2x−√10<0?
problems.idea: Complete the square.
steps: The integer x+1 can be −2,−1,0,1,2 only.

problems.title: An area ratio determines an angle
problems.question: A=50°, C is acute. M is midpoint of BC, MN⊥AC. Area ABC is eight times area MNC. Find B.
problems.idea: Express the two areas using BC=a, AC=b, and C.
formulas: Area ABC=ab sinC/2; area MNC=a²sinC cosC/8.
steps: Their ratio gives 4b/(a cosC)=8, hence b=2a cosC.
The cosine rule then gives c²=a²+b²−2ab cosC=a², so A=C.

problems.title: Which area cannot occur?
problems.question: Every side of a triangle lies strictly between 10 and 20. Which listed area is impossible: 0.005,150,1,200,64√3?
problems.idea: The largest area occurs in the limit of an equilateral triangle with side 20.
formulas: Δ≤(√3/4)L² for side bound L, so Δ<100√3<200.
steps: For completeness, isosceles triangles with base near 20 and equal legs between 10 and 20 have areas varying continuously from near zero to near 100√3.
Thus the other positive listed values, all below 100√3, can occur.
